items.summary: The Sixers are tied for the NBA’s best record at 14-3, but they still aren’t finishing off opponents the way an elite team should, writes Kris Rhim of ESPN. The latest example came Saturday afternoon against the one-win Bucks, as Philadelphia nearly squandered a 10-point lead with a little more than two minutes remaining. The game would have gone to overtime, but Tyler Herro’s three-pointer was ruled to be a split-second after the final buzzer (Twitter video link). “Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better,” LeBron James said. “But a team like that, we know they’re scrappy. items.summary: Rockets head coach Ime Udoka didn’t hide his disgust for his team’s effort following Friday’s NBA Cup loss in Denver, according to Varun Shankar of The Houston Chronicle. Udoka called the Rockets “mentally fragile” and was particularly critical of the defense, saying it lacked physicality, effort and “attention to detail.” In a back-and-forth contest with 32 lead changes and 17 ties, Houston was up five points with 5:10 remaining but was outscored 23-9 to close out the game. “You got to compete on (the defensive) end to give yourself a chance. You score 124, you should be able to win,” Udoka said. “But just count out the quarters. They had four 30-point quarters… you’re not going to win anything and that just shows a lack of effort, attention to detail or fight on that end.
